Premieres of these operas.Monteverdi's L'Orfeo: Premiered at the court of Mantua, it is among the oldest operas still regularly staged, and Orpheus charms the underworld with song.
Premieres of these operas.The Marriage of Figaro: Mozart's comedy was based on a banned play by Beaumarchais, and the librettist Da Ponte softened its politics to get it past the censors.
Premieres of these operas.The Magic Flute: It premiered about two months before Mozart's death, and he conducted one of its early performances from the keyboard.
Premieres of these operas.The Barber of Seville: Rossini's comic masterpiece was said to be written in a few weeks, and at the premiere supporters of a rival composer disrupted the show.
Premieres of these operas.La traviata: Verdi's opera flopped at its Venice premiere, partly because the soprano was too healthy-looking to play a consumptive heroine.
Premieres of these operas.Aida: It was commissioned for Cairo's opera house, but did not open the Suez Canal as is often claimed.
Premieres of these operas.La bohème: Puccini's tragedy of poor artists in Paris inspired the musical Rent, with its famous aria Che gelida manina.
Premieres of these operas.Madama Butterfly: The La Scala premiere was a disaster, with the audience jeering, and Puccini revised it extensively before it triumphed.
Premieres of these operas.Turandot: Puccini died with the opera unfinished, and at the first performance Toscanini stopped where the composer had stopped. Nessun dorma comes from it.
Premieres of these operas.Porgy and Bess: Gershwin's folk opera, set in Charleston, gave the world Summertime, and it was among the first major operas with an all-Black cast.

Steve Jobs's life and career.Co-founds Apple: Jobs co-founded Apple with Steve Wozniak in a garage, and they sold the first Apple I computers as bare circuit boards.
Steve Jobs's life and career.Unveils the Macintosh: The Macintosh arrived with a famous Super Bowl ad and brought the graphical interface and mouse to ordinary computer users.
Steve Jobs's life and career.Forced out of Apple: After a power struggle with the board and CEO John Sculley, Jobs left the company he co-founded and started NeXT.
Steve Jobs's life and career.Buys Pixar: Jobs bought the computer graphics division of Lucasfilm for about 10 million dollars, and he turned it into a film studio.
Steve Jobs's life and career.Toy Story released: The first fully computer-animated feature film was a huge hit and made Pixar a household name.
Steve Jobs's life and career.Returns to Apple: Apple bought Jobs's company NeXT, which brought him back, and he soon became chief executive and saved the firm.
Steve Jobs's life and career.Introduces the iPod: The original iPod put 1,000 songs in your pocket, and it helped Apple move beyond computers into consumer electronics.
Steve Jobs's life and career.Stanford commencement speech: Jobs told graduates to stay hungry and stay foolish, and talked about his firing and his cancer diagnosis.
Steve Jobs's life and career.Unveils the iPhone: Jobs introduced the phone as three products in one: an iPod, a phone and an internet communicator.
Steve Jobs's life and career.Steps down as CEO: Jobs stepped down because of failing health and died later that year, aged 56, from complications of pancreatic cancer.

Your genome by the numbers.DNA letters in a codon: Three-letter DNA words each name one amino acid or a stop signal.
Your genome by the numbers.Kinds of DNA base: Adenine, thymine, guanine and cytosine; Erwin Chargaff found in 1950 that the amounts of A and T match, as do G and C.
Your genome by the numbers.Standard amino acids: Two more, selenocysteine and pyrrolysine, are used rarely in some organisms.
Your genome by the numbers.Genes in mitochondrial DNA: Mitochondrial DNA is inherited almost exclusively from the mother, so it is used to trace maternal lineages.
Your genome by the numbers.Chromosomes in a cell: Humans have 23 pairs; chimpanzees have 48, because two ancestral chromosomes fused in our lineage.
Your genome by the numbers.Possible codons: With only 20 amino acids, most are encoded by several codons, and three codons are stop signals.
Your genome by the numbers.Base pairs in mitochondria: The standard Cambridge reference sequence for human mitochondrial DNA has 16,569 base pairs.
Your genome by the numbers.Protein-coding genes: They make up only 1 or 2 percent of the genome, a surprise of the Human Genome Project, which expected far more genes.
Your genome by the numbers.Base pairs in an egg cell: This is a haploid set; the Human Genome Project finished a draft by 2003, and a gapless version came in 2022.
Your genome by the numbers.Base pairs in a body cell: That is the paired set; stretched out, the DNA in a single cell would be about two metres long.

Units and places by area.Square foot: A square foot is a 12-inch square, and US real estate is priced and described in them.
Units and places by area.Square yard: Carpet in the US and UK is commonly sold by the square yard, which is nine square feet.
Units and places by area.Square metre: The metre was once defined as one ten-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the equator.
Units and places by area.Are: The are is a 10 by 10 metre square; mostly its hectare multiple, 100 ares, survives in use.
Units and places by area.Tennis court (doubles): A doubles court is 23.77 by 10.97 metres, wider than the singles court by 1.37 metres on each side.
Units and places by area.Acre: An acre was the land a yoke of oxen could plough in a day, and it is roughly three-quarters of a US football field.
Units and places by area.Soccer pitch: Soccer pitch sizes vary legally, and this figure matches the 105 by 68 metre international standard.
Units and places by area.Hectare: A hectare is a 100 metre square, about 1.4 soccer pitches, and is the standard unit for farmland and forests.
Units and places by area.Square kilometre: It equals 100 hectares, and Vatican City covers under half of one.
Units and places by area.Square mile: A square mile holds 640 acres, and the whole country of Monaco is smaller than one.

How high these fly.Cessna 172 (ceiling): The most-produced aircraft ever, with more than 40,000 built, is a training favourite.
How high these fly.Boeing 747 (cruising): Airliners cruise near this height because thinner air cuts drag while leaving enough oxygen for jet engines.
How high these fly.Concorde: At this altitude passengers could see the curve of Earth and a sky turning deep violet.
How high these fly.Lockheed U-2: Pilots must wear pressure suits like astronauts, because at this height the air pressure is too low to survive.
How high these fly.SR-71 Blackbird: It could outrun missiles at about Mach 3 and none was ever shot down in its career.
How high these fly.X-15 (record flight): Joe Walker's 1963 flight passed 100 km, the Karman line, which counts as spaceflight by international definition.
How high these fly.International Space Station: The station orbits at about 28,000 km/h and circles Earth roughly every 90 minutes.
How high these fly.GPS satellites: These satellites orbit twice a day, and relativity affects their clocks, so corrections are needed to stay accurate.
How high these fly.Geostationary satellites: At this height, one orbit takes exactly 24 hours, so a satellite hovers over the same spot, perfect for TV.
How high these fly.Apollo, out to the Moon: This is the Moon's average distance, which Apollo astronauts crossed in about three days.

How many of the small unit fit in the bi.Centimetres in an inch: The inch was fixed at exactly 2.54 cm in 1959 by international agreement.
How many of the small unit fit in the bi.Ounces in a pound: The abbreviation lb comes from the Latin libra, and oz from the Italian onza.
How many of the small unit fit in the bi.Inches in a yard: A legend says the yard was the distance from King Henry I's nose to his thumb.
How many of the small unit fit in the bi.Hours in a week: The seven-day week traces back to the Babylonians, who linked it to seven visible heavenly bodies.
How many of the small unit fit in the bi.Days in a leap year: The extra day is needed because Earth's orbit takes about 365.2422 days.
How many of the small unit fit in the bi.Millimetres in a metre: The metre was first defined as one ten-millionth of the distance from the pole to the equator.
How many of the small unit fit in the bi.Minutes in a day: We divide the day into 24 hours and 60 minutes thanks to ancient Egyptian and Babylonian numeral systems.
How many of the small unit fit in the bi.Seconds in an hour: The second is now defined by a caesium atom's vibrations, 9,192,631,770 of them.
How many of the small unit fit in the bi.Feet in a mile: A 1593 English law set the mile at eight furlongs, which fixed it at 5,280 feet.
How many of the small unit fit in the bi.Seconds in a day: Because Earth's rotation is uneven, days are occasionally given a leap second to stay in sync.

Diameter: from a pea to a planet.A garden pea: Gregor Mendel grew thousands of pea plants in his monastery garden to uncover the basic laws of inheritance.
Diameter: from a pea to a planet.A marble: Marbles have been rolled since antiquity, but machine-made glass marbles only took off in the early 1900s.
Diameter: from a pea to a planet.A ping-pong ball: Table tennis balls grew from 38 to 40 mm in 2000, which slowed the ball and made rallies longer for television.
Diameter: from a pea to a planet.A pool ball: Billiard balls were once carved from ivory, and the search for a substitute helped drive the invention of early plastics such as celluloid.
Diameter: from a pea to a planet.A tennis ball: Tennis balls are fuzzy because the felt slows them through the air; the yellow colour was adopted in 1972 so they show up on TV.
Diameter: from a pea to a planet.A softball: Softballs are in fact hard; the game began in 1887 as an indoor Chicago version of baseball, first played with a boxing glove.
Diameter: from a pea to a planet.A bowling ball: Ten-pin rules cap the ball at about 8.6 inches across, with a weight limit of 16 pounds.
Diameter: from a pea to a planet.An exercise ball: Often called a Swiss ball because Swiss physiotherapists used big balls like this in rehabilitation in the 1960s.
Diameter: from a pea to a planet.The Moon: At about a quarter of Earth's width, the Moon is large for a moon, and roughly as wide as Australia.
Diameter: from a pea to a planet.Earth: Earth bulges at the equator, so it is about 43 km wider there than pole to pole because of its spin.

Latin numbers, by the value they name.tres: Tres lives on in Spanish and Italian 'tre', and Latin 'tres' gave English the words 'trio' and 'triple'.
Latin numbers, by the value they name.quinque: Quinque gives us 'quintet' and 'quintessence', which literally meant the 'fifth essence'.
Latin numbers, by the value they name.sex: A sextant is named for the sixth of a circle, 60 degrees, that its arc covers when measuring a star's angle.
Latin numbers, by the value they name.septem: September means 'seventh month', named when the Roman year began in March, and the name stayed after January and February were added.
Latin numbers, by the value they name.octo: October once was the eighth month; the name stuck even after the calendar moved, as 'octave' also nods to eight.
Latin numbers, by the value they name.novem: November was the ninth month of the Roman calendar, which began in March, so the numbers lag by two.
Latin numbers, by the value they name.decem: Decem gives us 'decimate', which originally meant killing one soldier in every ten as a Roman punishment.
Latin numbers, by the value they name.viginti: Viginti is the source of French vingt and Italian venti, and of the word 'vicennial' for every twenty years.
Latin numbers, by the value they name.centum: Centum gives 'century' and 'percent'; a Roman centurion actually led about 80 soldiers, not 100.
Latin numbers, by the value they name.mille: Mille gave us 'mile', from mille passus, 'a thousand paces', the distance a Roman legion's soldiers measured by walking.

Milestones of the US civil rights strugg.Dred Scott decision: The Supreme Court ruled that Black Americans, free or enslaved, could not be citizens. The decision helped push the nation toward the Civil War.
Milestones of the US civil rights strugg.Plessy v. Ferguson: The ruling upheld "separate but equal" segregation. It stood for nearly six decades, until it was overturned in the 1950s.
Milestones of the US civil rights strugg.NAACP founded: Founded by a group of Black and white activists, including W.E.B. Du Bois, partly in response to a 1908 race riot in Springfield, Illinois.
Milestones of the US civil rights strugg.Jackie Robinson's MLB debut: He broke baseball's color line with the Brooklyn Dodgers, and his number 42 is retired across the major leagues, the only number retired league-wide.
Milestones of the US civil rights strugg.Brown v. Board of Education: The Supreme Court unanimously ruled segregated public schools unconstitutional, overturning Plessy's "separate but equal" doctrine in education.
Milestones of the US civil rights strugg.Montgomery Bus Boycott: It began when Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat, and it lasted 381 days, with Martin Luther King Jr. emerging as a national leader.
Milestones of the US civil rights strugg.Little Rock Nine: Nine Black students integrated an Arkansas high school, with President Eisenhower sending federal troops to protect them from a mob.
Milestones of the US civil rights strugg.March on Washington: Over 200,000 people gathered at the Lincoln Memorial, where Martin Luther King Jr. gave his "I Have a Dream" speech.
Milestones of the US civil rights strugg.Voting Rights Act: Signed by President Lyndon Johnson, it banned racial discrimination in voting, such as literacy tests, after the marches in Selma, Alabama.
Milestones of the US civil rights strugg.Obama elected president: Barack Obama became the first Black president of the United States, winning the election on November 4, 2008.

When these civilizations began.Sumerian cities: The city of Uruk was one of the world's first; Sumerians also invented cuneiform writing.
When these civilizations began.Unified Egypt: Tradition credits a king, Narmer or Menes, with joining Upper and Lower Egypt into one kingdom.
When these civilizations began.Indus Valley cities: Cities such as Mohenjo-daro had grid layouts and drains; its script remains undeciphered.
When these civilizations began.Minoan palaces of Crete: Named after the legendary King Minos, they built palaces such as Knossos, adorned with frescoes of bull-leaping.
When these civilizations began.Shang China: Its oracle bones are the earliest known Chinese writing, and its artisans made fine bronzes.
When these civilizations began.Olmecs: This early Mesoamerican culture carved colossal stone heads and is often called the 'mother culture' of the region.
When these civilizations began.Archaic Greece: The first Olympic Games were traditionally held in 776 BC; Homer's epics took shape around this time.
When these civilizations began.Roman Republic: Romans overthrew their last king, Tarquin, and ran the state through elected officials and a Senate.
When these civilizations began.Classic Maya: Maya astronomers tracked Venus and eclipses, and cities like Tikal had hieroglyphic inscriptions.
When these civilizations began.Aztec Tenochtitlan: Founded on an island in Lake Texcoco, the city lies beneath modern Mexico City.

Legendary endurance feats and races, by.Pheidippides's run (legend): Herodotus says he ran from Athens to Sparta, some 240 km, seeking help; the marathon run is a later legend.
Legendary endurance feats and races, by.Barclay's 1,000 miles: In 1809 Captain Barclay walked 1,000 miles in 1,000 hours, one mile each hour.
Legendary endurance feats and races, by.First Olympic marathon: Greek Spyridon Louis won in Athens; the 26.2-mile distance was set in London in 1908.
Legendary endurance feats and races, by.First Tour de France: The race was created to boost newspaper L'Auto's sales; Maurice Garin won the first.
Legendary endurance feats and races, by.First Comrades Marathon: South Africa's ultramarathon, about 90 km between Durban and Pietermaritzburg, began as a memorial to WWI soldiers.
Legendary endurance feats and races, by.Western States 100 born: It began when Gordy Ainsleigh ran the course after his horse went lame in a horse race.
Legendary endurance feats and races, by.First Ironman triathlon: Held in Honolulu with 15 starters; 12 finished, and Gordon Haller won.
Legendary endurance feats and races, by.First Spartathlon: The 246 km race from Athens to Sparta follows the route of the Greek messenger described by Herodotus.
Legendary endurance feats and races, by.Messner climbs all 14 8,000ers: He was the first to climb all fourteen 8,000-metre peaks, without supplemental oxygen.
Legendary endurance feats and races, by.Edgley swims around Britain: Ross Edgley swam about 1,780 miles around Britain in 157 days, suffering jellyfish stings and a damaged tongue from salt water.

Avengers actors by birth year.Samuel L. Jackson: His Nick Fury in the comics was redrawn to look like him, and he later signed to play Fury across many films.
His Iron Man in 2008 launched the whole Marvel Cinematic Universe and revived a career that had been in trouble.
Avengers actors by birth year.Mark Ruffalo: He took over the Hulk from Edward Norton and also does the motion capture, so the Hulk moves like him.
Avengers actors by birth year.Paul Rudd: He helped rewrite the script for Ant-Man with Adam McKay, and before that he played the lovable Josh in Clueless.
Avengers actors by birth year.Jeremy Renner: He earned two Oscar nominations before Hawkeye, for The Hurt Locker and The Town.
Avengers actors by birth year.Benedict Cumberbatch: He also plays Sherlock Holmes on TV and voiced the dragon Smaug in The Hobbit films.
Avengers actors by birth year.Chris Hemsworth: Before Thor, the Australian actor was in the soap opera Home and Away.
Avengers actors by birth year.Scarlett Johansson: She also voiced the AI Samantha in Her, and Lost in Translation was her breakthrough film.
Avengers actors by birth year.Elizabeth Olsen: She is the younger sister of Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen, and a distinguished actor in her own right.
Avengers actors by birth year.Tom Holland: He began on the London stage as the title role in Billy Elliot the Musical before swinging into the Spider-Man suit.

Britain's wildest weather, in order.Great Frost (Thames freezes): In the Little Ice Age, the river froze hard enough for fairs, with ice-skating, ox roasts and printing presses on the ice.
Britain's wildest weather, in order.Tay Bridge storm: A gale in 1879 blew over the Tay Rail Bridge in Scotland, while a train was crossing, and the disaster killed about 75.
Britain's wildest weather, in order.Post-war winter of deep snow: The winter of 1947 brought weeks of snow to Britain, and fuel shortages, in a country still rebuilding after the war.
Britain's wildest weather, in order.Lynmouth flood: Heavy rain on Exmoor sent a wall of water through the Devon village, and the disaster killed 34 people.
Britain's wildest weather, in order.North Sea flood: A surge down the North Sea flooded the east coast, killing over 300 in England, and led to the Thames Barrier.
Britain's wildest weather, in order.The Big Freeze: A winter so cold the sea froze at the edges, with ice on the shore, the coldest in Britain for over 200 years.
Britain's wildest weather, in order.The Great Drought: A summer so dry reservoirs ran low, and the government appointed a Minister for Drought, followed by heavy rain days later.
Britain's wildest weather, in order.Boscastle flood: Torrential rain turned a small Cornish river into a torrent, and helicopters rescued around 100 people, though nobody died.
Britain's wildest weather, in order.Storm Desmond: A storm that flooded Cumbria and Lancashire, bringing a record 341 mm of rain in 24 hours at Honister Pass.
Britain's wildest weather, in order.First 40 °C heatwave: In July 2022 Britain officially passed 40 C for the first time, with 40.3 C recorded at Coningsby in Lincolnshire.

More sporting firsts: when these began.Winter Olympics: Held at Chamonix, it was first called 'International Winter Sports Week' and only later named the first Winter Olympics.
More sporting firsts: when these began.F1 World Championship: Britain's Silverstone hosted the opener, and Giuseppe Farina became the first world champion in an Alfa Romeo.
More sporting firsts: when these began.Paralympic Games: Founded by Ludwig Guttmann after World War II, it grew out of a sports festival for wounded veterans at Stoke Mandeville.
More sporting firsts: when these began.Super Bowl: It began as a championship game between the NFL and AFL champions, and the name 'Super Bowl' came from a child's toy.
More sporting firsts: when these began.Men's Cricket World Cup: The first tournament, held in England, was won by the West Indies, in 60-over one-day games.
More sporting firsts: when these began.Rugby World Cup: Co-hosted by Australia and New Zealand, the first edition was won by New Zealand's All Blacks.
More sporting firsts: when these began.FIFA Women's World Cup: The first tournament, in China, was won by the United States, which has dominated since.
More sporting firsts: when these began.X Games: The extreme-sports festival launched by ESPN, where skateboarders, BMX riders and others compete.
More sporting firsts: when these began.WNBA's first season: The women's pro basketball league tipped off in 1997, a year after the US women's Olympic team won gold in Atlanta.
More sporting firsts: when these began.First T20 international: The shortest cricket format debuted when Australia met New Zealand in 2005, in a match where players wore retro kits for fun.

When these sports video games came out.Tennis for Two: Built at a US nuclear lab to entertain visitors, it displayed a ball on an oscilloscope and is one of the earliest video games.
When these sports video games came out.Pole Position: It was among the first racing games to use a real track, Fuji, and made players qualify before racing.
When these sports video games came out.Track and Field: Players pounded buttons to run faster, and the mashing was so brutal that arcades reportedly lost buttons to it.
When these sports video games came out.Punch-Out!!: The boxing game's hero, Little Mac, trains in a gym, and the series later got a Mike Tyson edition.
When these sports video games came out.Tecmo Bowl: It carried the players' union license, so real NFL stars were in it without their names, and it became a cult favorite on the NES.
When these sports video games came out.John Madden Football: Named after the broadcaster and coach, who insisted on a game with eleven players a side instead of a simplified version.
When these sports video games came out.FIFA International Soccer: EA's first soccer game, it had no official player names to begin with, but it started the annual series that continues today.
When these sports video games came out.Tony Hawk's Pro Skater: A skateboarding game that turned a niche sport into a mainstream hit, it was famous for its soundtrack and its combos.
When these sports video games came out.Wii Sports: Bundled with the Wii, it let players swing the remote for bowling and tennis, making it one of the best-selling video games of all time.
When these sports video games came out.Rocket League: Imagine soccer played by rocket-powered cars; it was released by Psyonix and later went free to play.

Milestones of the environmental movement.Keeling CO₂ record begins: A scientist on Hawaii's Mauna Loa began measuring carbon dioxide, giving the famous Keeling Curve of rising levels.
Milestones of the environmental movement.Silent Spring published: Rachel Carson's book on pesticides like DDT helped launch the modern environmental movement.
Milestones of the environmental movement.First Earth Day: About 20 million Americans took part in the first one, on April 22, and it led to creation of the EPA the same year.
Milestones of the environmental movement.UN Stockholm conference: It was the first major UN conference on the environment, and it created the UN Environment Programme.
Milestones of the environmental movement.Ozone hole reported: British scientists reported a hole in the ozone layer over Antarctica, caused by chemicals used in fridges and sprays.
Milestones of the environmental movement.Montreal Protocol: It phased out ozone-damaging chemicals, and is often called the most successful environmental treaty ever.
Milestones of the environmental movement.IPCC founded: This UN-backed panel of scientists produces regular reports assessing climate change.
Milestones of the environmental movement.Rio Earth Summit: The summit in Brazil produced the UN's climate convention and a treaty on biodiversity.
Milestones of the environmental movement.Kyoto Protocol: It set binding emissions targets for rich countries, and came into force in 2005 after long delays.
Milestones of the environmental movement.Paris Agreement: Almost every country agreed to limit warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.

Balls (and one shuttlecock) by weight.Table tennis ball: A table tennis ball is a hollow celluloid or plastic sphere, and the sport switched from 38 to 40 mm balls in 2000 to slow rallies.
Balls (and one shuttlecock) by weight.Shuttlecock: Shuttlecocks are made from goose feathers, and top-level players can smash them faster than 400 km/h.
Balls (and one shuttlecock) by weight.Golf ball: The golf ball's dimples, usually 300 to 500, reduce drag and let the ball fly farther.
Balls (and one shuttlecock) by weight.Tennis ball: Tennis balls were white until 1972, when yellow was introduced to be more visible on TV.
Balls (and one shuttlecock) by weight.Baseball: A baseball has 108 double stitches, and each is sewn by hand.
Balls (and one shuttlecock) by weight.Softball: Despite its name, a softball is hard, and it was invented in Chicago in 1887 as an indoor game.
Balls (and one shuttlecock) by weight.Volleyball: Volleyballs were first designed by William Morgan in 1895 as a gentler alternative to basketball.
Balls (and one shuttlecock) by weight.Soccer ball: Soccer balls traditionally had 32 panels, 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons, a shape called a truncated icosahedron.
Balls (and one shuttlecock) by weight.Basketball: The first basketballs were brown, and James Naismith's game used peach baskets and a soccer ball.
Balls (and one shuttlecock) by weight.Bowling ball: Bowling balls of 16 pounds, or 7.26 kg, are the maximum, and the finger holes are drilled to fit each player's hand.

The road to discovering vitamins.Lind's scurvy trial: James Lind's trial aboard HMS Salisbury found that citrus fruit cured sailors, but the navy took decades to issue lemon juice.
The road to discovering vitamins.Eijkman links rice to beriberi: A Dutch doctor in Java noticed chickens fed polished rice got a beriberi-like illness, and he shared a Nobel Prize in 1929.
The road to discovering vitamins.Funk coins vitamine: Casimir Funk called them 'vital amines', and the 'e' was later dropped when not all turned out to be amines.
The road to discovering vitamins.Vitamin A discovered: It was found as a fat-soluble factor in butter and egg yolk that animals needed to grow, and it protects eyesight.
The road to discovering vitamins.Vitamin D named: Cod liver oil helped it be identified as the cure for rickets, in which children's bones stay soft.
The road to discovering vitamins.Thiamine isolated: This was the first B vitamin to be purified, from rice bran, and it prevents beriberi.
The road to discovering vitamins.Vitamin K discovered: Henrik Dam found it while studying chickens that bled easily; the K stands for the German Koagulation.
The road to discovering vitamins.Vitamin C identified: Albert Szent-Gyorgyi, who won a Nobel for his work, first isolated it from paprika.
The road to discovering vitamins.Folic acid isolated: The name comes from the Latin for leaf, since it was isolated from spinach, and it is now added to flour to prevent birth defects.
The road to discovering vitamins.Vitamin B12 isolated: The red crystals contain cobalt, and the discovery turned pernicious anaemia, once fatal, into a treatable condition.

Asian countries by population.Bhutan: This Himalayan kingdom famously measures national progress by Gross National Happiness rather than only GDP.
Asian countries by population.Mongolia: There are more horses than people here, and about half the population lives in the capital, Ulaanbaatar.
Asian countries by population.Sri Lanka: It is the world's leading source of Ceylon tea, and the island was once known as Ceylon.
Asian countries by population.Malaysia: The country is split in two by the South China Sea, with one part on the Malay Peninsula and the other on Borneo.
Asian countries by population.South Korea: About half the people live in the Seoul region, one of the densest urban areas on Earth.
Asian countries by population.Thailand: It is the only Southeast Asian country never colonised by a European power.
Asian countries by population.Vietnam: It is shaped like an S, and it is the world's second-largest coffee producer.
Asian countries by population.Japan: Its population has been shrinking since around 2008, with more elderly than young.
Asian countries by population.Bangladesh: Most of the people live on the delta of the Ganges and Brahmaputra rivers, about the size of Iowa.
Asian countries by population.Indonesia: The fourth most populous country in the world is spread across more than 17,000 islands.

Michael Jackson singles, in order.ABC (Jackson 5): The Jackson 5 hit knocked The Beatles' 'Let It Be' off the top of the US chart in 1970, with a 12-year-old Michael on lead.
Michael Jackson singles, in order.Ben: This tender song about a pet rat was the title track of a sequel to a horror film, and it hit number one when Michael was only 14.
Michael Jackson singles, in order.Don't Stop 'Til You Get Enough: The Off the Wall opener earned Michael his first solo Grammy, and helped break him out of the shadow of his Motown childhood.
Michael Jackson singles, in order.Beat It: Eddie Van Halen played the blistering guitar solo for free, after Quincy Jones asked him to. It is credited only as a favour.
Michael Jackson singles, in order.Bad: Martin Scorsese directed the long black-and-white video, set in a New York subway, which ran closer to a short film than a clip.
Michael Jackson singles, in order.Black or White: Its video's face-morphing sequence was cutting-edge computer animation, and guitarist Slash played the screaming solo.
Michael Jackson singles, in order.Scream: He recorded it as a duet with his sister Janet. The pricey space-station video is often cited as one of the most expensive ever made.
Michael Jackson singles, in order.You Rock My World: Its video features Chris Tucker and Marlon Brando, and the song came from his 2001 album Invincible, his last full studio release.
Michael Jackson singles, in order.This Is It: Released after his death, it began as a demo he co-wrote with Paul Anka decades earlier, and gained new life tied to his planned London shows.
Michael Jackson singles, in order.Love Never Felt So Good: Co-written with Paul Anka, it came out on the Xscape album, a set of reworked unreleased recordings.

When these famous brands were founded.Beretta: Beretta, a gunmaker in Italy, claims to be one of the oldest family businesses in the world, and it is still run by the same family.
When these famous brands were founded.Twinings: Twinings opened its Strand tearoom in London in 1706, and the same shop is still there today.
When these famous brands were founded.Guinness: Arthur Guinness signed a 9,000-year lease on a Dublin brewery for just 45 pounds a year, and his stout became Ireland's best known drink.
Levi Strauss sold dry goods in San Francisco. Riveted denim trousers came in 1873, with tailor Jacob Davis.
When these famous brands were founded.Coca-Cola: Pharmacist John Pemberton first made Coca-Cola in Atlanta as a medicinal syrup, and it was first sold at a soda fountain.
When these famous brands were founded.Harley-Davidson: Harley-Davidson began in a tiny Milwaukee shed, and by 1920 it was one of the world's biggest motorcycle makers.
When these famous brands were founded.Samsung: Samsung means three stars in Korean. It started as a trading company selling dried fish, fruit and noodles.
When these famous brands were founded.IKEA: IKEA stands for founder Ingvar Kamprad's initials plus Elmtaryd farm and Agunnaryd village, where he grew up.
When these famous brands were founded.Apple: Apple was founded by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne. Wayne sold his share back within weeks for a few hundred dollars.
When these famous brands were founded.Google: Google began as a Stanford research project called BackRub, and its name is a play on googol, a 1 followed by 100 zeros.

Original launch prices.Glass of Coca-Cola (1886): Coca-Cola was originally 5 cents a glass, and sold at Jacobs' Pharmacy soda fountain in Atlanta, averaging only nine glasses a day.
Original launch prices.McDonald's hamburger (1948): The McDonald brothers sold hamburgers for 15 cents in San Bernardino, and they pioneered the fast-food assembly line.
Original launch prices.Big Mac (1967): The Big Mac was created by franchisee Jim Delligatti in Pittsburgh, and it spread nationwide in 1968.
Original launch prices.Game Boy: The Game Boy came with Tetris, and it was cheaper than rivals, despite a monochrome screen.
Original launch prices.PlayStation (US): The PlayStation launched in the US in 1995 at 299 dollars, and it undercut the rival Sega Saturn.
Original launch prices.iPhone (2007): The first iPhone launched at 499 dollars with a contract, and Steve Jobs called it a revolutionary product.
Original launch prices.Apple I: The Apple I sold for $666.66, since Steve Wozniak liked repeating digits, and it came as a bare circuit board.
Original launch prices.Ford Model T: The Ford Model T launched in 1908 at 850 dollars, and price cuts later brought it below 300 dollars.
Original launch prices.Macintosh (1984): The original Macintosh was introduced in a Super Bowl ad, and it was famous for its graphical interface and mouse.
Original launch prices.Motorola DynaTAC phone: The DynaTAC 8000X weighed about a kilogram and needed ten hours to charge for a half-hour of talk time.

From a grain of sand to a supergiant: si.Grain of sand: Geologists define sand by size, between about 0.06 and 2 mm, so this is a mid-sized grain.
From a grain of sand to a supergiant: si.Adult human: You shrink about a centimetre during the day as the discs in your spine compress, and recover overnight.
From a grain of sand to a supergiant: si.Blue whale (length): The largest animal known to have lived. Its tongue alone can weigh about as much as an elephant.
From a grain of sand to a supergiant: si.Mount Everest (height): Nepal and China measured it as 8,848.86 m in 2020. It rises a few millimetres each year as the plates push.
From a grain of sand to a supergiant: si.Ceres: The largest object in the asteroid belt, a dwarf planet that holds around a third of the belt's total mass.
From a grain of sand to a supergiant: si.The Moon: About a quarter of Earth's width. The Moon is drifting away by about 3.8 cm a year.
From a grain of sand to a supergiant: si.Earth: Earth's equator bulges, so it is about 43 km wider than from pole to pole.
From a grain of sand to a supergiant: si.Jupiter: More than 1,300 Earths would fit inside, and its Great Red Spot is a storm that has raged for centuries.
From a grain of sand to a supergiant: si.The Sun: It holds 99.8 percent of the solar system's mass. About 1.3 million Earths would fit inside it.
From a grain of sand to a supergiant: si.Betelgeuse: A red supergiant in Orion that could someday explode as a supernova. Placed at our Sun's spot, it would swallow the inner planets.

Iceland's eruptions, in order.Laki: A fissure eruption whose toxic gas killed about a fifth of Iceland's people and brought cold summers across Europe.
Iceland's eruptions, in order.Askja: The 1875 eruption dusted Norway with ash and drove many Icelanders to emigrate to Canada.
Iceland's eruptions, in order.Hekla: Medieval Europeans called it the gateway to hell. It was quiet for about a century before 1947.
Iceland's eruptions, in order.Surtsey: A new island born from the sea off Iceland's south coast. Scientists have watched life colonise it ever since.
Iceland's eruptions, in order.Eldfell (Heimaey): Lava threatened the harbour of Heimaey's town, and islanders sprayed seawater to cool it and save the port.
Iceland's eruptions, in order.Gjálp (under Vatnajökull): An eruption under the ice melted it and caused a huge glacial flood, a jökulhlaup, in 1996.
Iceland's eruptions, in order.Eyjafjallajökull: The ash cloud grounded flights across Europe for days, affecting millions of passengers.
Iceland's eruptions, in order.Holuhraun: A lava field that was Iceland's biggest eruption in over 200 years, since Laki.
Iceland's eruptions, in order.Fagradalsfjall: It erupted in a valley near Reykjavik and drew crowds of hikers to watch the lava, ending after six months.
Iceland's eruptions, in order.Sundhnúkur (Grindavík): One of a series of eruptions that forced the evacuation of the town of Grindavík in November 2023.

How cold is it?.Absolute zero: Absolute zero is where particles have minimal motion. Scientists have gotten within billionths of a degree, but can never quite reach it.
How cold is it?.Deep space: The cosmic microwave background, leftover glow from the Big Bang, sets space's temperature at about 2.7 K. That is only a little above absolute zero.
How cold is it?.Surface of Pluto: New Horizons flew by in 2015 and found a vast heart-shaped nitrogen glacier. The dwarf planet is also home to icy mountains.
How cold is it?.Liquid nitrogen: Liquid nitrogen is used for freezing food, treating warts and making instant ice cream. It boils away at room temperature.
How cold is it?.Coldest on Earth (Vostok): The Antarctic station Vostok recorded this on 21 July 1983. Satellites later measured even colder, about -93 °C, elsewhere on the ice sheet.
How cold is it?.Dry ice: Dry ice is frozen carbon dioxide, and it turns straight to gas without melting. That is why it makes fog in spooky stage effects.
How cold is it?.Average day on Mars: Mars's thin air can't hold heat, so temperatures swing wildly. Daily averages like this hide nights far colder.
How cold is it?.Mercury freezes: Mercury is the only metal liquid at room temperature, which is why old thermometers used it. It freezes solid at about -39 °C.
How cold is it?.Home freezer: Home freezers run at about 0 °F, which happens to be this value. It is cold enough to stop bacteria from growing, though not killing them.
How cold is it?.Water freezes: The Celsius scale uses this as zero, and 100 for boiling. Anders Celsius originally had it the other way round, with boiling at zero.

How tall are these landmarks?.Leaning Tower of Pisa: It began leaning during construction because of soft ground; engineers cut its tilt in the 1990s and 2000s.
How tall are these landmarks?.Taj Mahal: Shah Jahan built it for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, and its four minarets lean slightly outward, so they would fall away from the tomb in a quake.
How tall are these landmarks?.Statue of Liberty (with base): Its copper skin is only about as thick as two pennies, and its green color is natural oxidation.
How tall are these landmarks?.St Paul's Cathedral: Christopher Wren's dome kept it London's tallest building until 1967.
How tall are these landmarks?.Great Pyramid (today): It was the tallest human-made structure for about 3,800 years, and it has lost its top and polished casing since.
How tall are these landmarks?.Washington Monument: This obelisk is the world's tallest stone structure, capped with aluminium, then a precious metal.
How tall are these landmarks?.Eiffel Tower: Heat makes its iron expand, so it grows up to about 15 cm taller in summer.
How tall are these landmarks?.Empire State (to tip): It was built in 1931 in just 410 days, with thousands of workers.
How tall are these landmarks?.CN Tower: It was the world's tallest freestanding structure from 1976 until 2007.
How tall are these landmarks?.Burj Khalifa: It opened in 2010, and has over 160 floors, so tall that the sun sets at different times at the top and the bottom.

A salmon's life, step by step.Eggs laid in river gravel: The female digs a nest, called a redd, in clean gravel with her tail. Cold, oxygen-rich flowing water is essential for the eggs to survive.
A salmon's life, step by step.Hatches with a yolk sac: Newly hatched young, called alevins, stay hidden in the gravel and live off the yolk sac attached to their belly.
A salmon's life, step by step.Tiny fry start to feed: After the yolk runs out, the fry emerge and begin to catch tiny insects. Only a small fraction of eggs will survive to adulthood.
A salmon's life, step by step.Young parr grow in the river: Parr have dark bars on their sides for camouflage in the stream. They stay in fresh water for a year or more before heading downstream.
A salmon's life, step by step.Turns silver as a smolt: The change to silver coloration, and changes in body chemistry, prepare the young fish for life in salt water.
A salmon's life, step by step.Swims out to sea: Smolts head downstream in spring, often in big groups. They travel hundreds or even thousands of kilometres to feeding grounds in the ocean.
A salmon's life, step by step.Grows big feeding at sea: At sea, salmon feed on small fish and shrimp and grow rapidly, often multiplying their weight many times over a year or two.
A salmon's life, step by step.Returns to its home river: Salmon find their birth river by smell and Earth's magnetic cues. They stop eating as they swim upstream, relying on stored fat.
A salmon's life, step by step.Leaps up waterfalls: Salmon can leap heights of well over two metres to clear obstacles. Fish ladders help them pass dams.
A salmon's life, step by step.Spawns where it hatched: Pacific salmon die after spawning, and their bodies feed the forest, while Atlantic salmon may survive to spawn more than once.

Pirates, real and fictional.Henry Morgan sacks Panama: Welsh privateer Henry Morgan, later knighted and made Lieutenant Governor of Jamaica, sacked Panama City.
Pirates, real and fictional.Captain Kidd hanged: Captain William Kidd was hanged in London, and his supposed buried treasure inspired legends.
Pirates, real and fictional.Blackbeard killed: Edward Teach lit slow-burning fuses under his hat to look demonic, and was killed by Lieutenant Robert Maynard off North Carolina.
Pirates, real and fictional.Black Bart killed: Bartholomew Roberts captured over 400 ships, making him the most successful pirate of the golden age.
Pirates, real and fictional.Ching Shih surrenders: She commanded around 1,500 ships and tens of thousands of pirates, and unusually retired peacefully.
Pirates, real and fictional.Treasure Island: Robert Louis Stevenson drew a map for his stepson, and Long John Silver gave us the image of the parrot-carrying pirate.
Pirates, real and fictional.Peter Pan play: J.M. Barrie's play introduced Captain Hook, and the same actor traditionally plays Hook and Mr. Darling.
Pirates, real and fictional.Disneyland Pirates ride: Walt Disney oversaw its design but did not live to see it open in New Orleans Square.
Pirates, real and fictional.Talk Like a Pirate Day begins: It was started by two friends in Oregon, John Baur and Mark Summers, and popularised by humorist Dave Barry.
Pirates, real and fictional.Pirates of the Caribbean film: Johnny Depp's Captain Jack Sparrow earned him an Oscar nomination, in a film based on a theme park ride.
